items.summary: fix(telegram): keep pending questions when settings commands arrive (#168004) The Telegram ingress supersede predicate let any recognized command or bot_command entity discard pending pre-adoption input, so a question followed within about half a second by /verbose, /think, /usage or /reasoning was silently dropped. Only authorized stop requests and /new or /reset may now cancel pending input; every other command waits behind it. Found by our Telegram Test Server bug hunt. Related #166504. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: docs(apple): document orphaned WebSocket upgrades on cancellation (#1…
items.summary: docs(apple): document orphaned WebSocket upgrades on cancellation (#168003) Cancelling a URLSessionWebSocketTask just as its HTTP 101 arrives can complete the task as cancelled and then open the upgraded socket anyway. No URLSession API reclaims that socket; generation and admission fencing keep it unused and the Gateway closes its end at the preauth timeout. Document that at WebSocketTaskBox.cancel, and correct the fleet comment: session invalidation releases the delegate and idle connections but cannot reclaim the orphan. Proof: headless URLSession probe leaked 3-8/100 near-simultaneous cancels across every client-side variant; transport probe through GatewayNodeSession + GatewayTLSPinningSession leaked 13/300 with zero connect frames, routes, or reconnects on orphans. OpenClawKit builds; SwiftFormat and SwiftLint clean.

items.title: fix(openai): ChatGPT-only model list offers unlisted pro models that …
items.summary: fix(openai): ChatGPT-only model list offers unlisted pro models that fail (#167975) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: for a user signed in with only a ChatGPT account, the default model list offers `openai/gpt-5.4-pro` and `openai/gpt-5.5-pro` even though that account's model listing doesn't include them, so choosing either one fails. ## User Impact ChatGPT-only users stop seeing these two models in the default model view (TUI and the Gateway `models.list` default view). Models the account lists stay, and so do hidden rows the account is entitled to, such as `gpt-5.5`. A user who also has an OpenAI API key still sees both pro models. ## Why This Change Was Made - A successful ChatGPT account listing now records every model id it returned, hidden rows included, as private `listedModelIds` on the ready provider outcome. The public `providerOutcomes` projection still carries only provider, profile and status. - The picker's availability check uses that list. A model served both by an API key and by ChatGPT, but missing from the account's listing, can't be used through the ChatGPT account. It stays available only if a usable non-subscription credential exists. - The list applies only to the credential that made it. The check reads the ready outcome whose `profileId` matches the selected ChatGPT profile; another account's listing never narrows or widens it, and a profile with no ready listing of its own keeps today's behavior. - When the model is unavailable, no reason code is attached, so the UI and `/models` show a neutral "Unavailable" instead of "Sign-in needed" or "add a key". The user is signed in; this account just doesn't have the model. - This change covers the picker only. If someone types an unlisted id by hand, the request can still reach OpenAI and fail with OpenAI's own error. - To stay within the line-cap ratchet, two pieces moved: the runtime credential overlay now lives in `model-auth-availability.runtime-overlay.ts`, and the ready-outcome builder now lives in `extensions/openai/model-service-tiers.ts`. Neither move changes behavior. ## Evidence Real ChatGPT account (device-code sign-in), isolated profile, loopback Gateway. Same profile, main build `d0fc39e` vs this branch `f53ad9c`: | Gateway `models.list` view=default, provider openai | main | branch | |---|---|---| | ChatGPT-only | 11 rows: 8 listed + `gpt-5.4-pro`, `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.5-pro` | 9 rows: 8 listed + `gpt-5.5` | | ChatGPT + OpenAI API key (control) | n/a | `gpt-5.4-pro`, `gpt-5.5-pro` present and available | `openclaw models list --provider openai --plain` (configured view) showed the same 8 listed rows on both builds; that view was never affected. - Regression: `src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.test.ts` "with a ChatGPT account listing". An unlisted dual-route id is unavailable with no reason code. A hidden listed id stays available. With an API key, or when the listing is unavailable, the subscription route is kept. - Multi-account regression (same file, "uses only the selected account's listing"): profiles A and B, A's ready listing omits `gpt-5.5-pro` and `gpt-5.5`, B selected. B with no outcome or an unavailable outcome keeps the subscription route; B's own listing that includes the model keeps it available; B's own listing that omits it makes it unavailable even when a third account lists it. The no-observation, unavailable, and omits cases fail on `de076ec6362` and pass on the fix. The real-account run above was not repeated: the OpenAI catalog hook already stamps the ready outcome with the discovering profile's id (`projectOpenAICatalog`), which is the selected profile in the single-account case, so that path is unchanged. - Provider: `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts`: `listedModelIds` includes hidden rows. - Suites: model-auth-availability (4 files), model-catalog-decisions, model-catalog-service-tiers, openai-provider (3 files), models-list-result.provider-outcomes. All pass. - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes. This includes the line-cap ratchet, tsgo core and core tests, and plugin boundaries. `oxlint --type-aware` is clean on the changed files. ## Merge Danger - Adds an optional `listedModelIds` field to `ProviderCatalogOutcome` (the plugin SDK `provider-catalog-shared` type). The change is additive and documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/model-catalogs.md` as private provenance that is never projected publicly. - Touches `src/agents/model-auth-availability.ts`, which has prior history from pash-openai (`4573635c77f`). That history includes `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts`. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: 當威脅情報只剩大量數據，企業該相信什麼？
items.summary: 生成式AI降低了偵察、釣魚郵件撰寫及部分程式開發工作的門檻，使攻擊者得以更快、更大量地展開行動，企業導入模型、資料集、套件與AI工具後，擴大了軟體及AI供應鏈的風險。 這兩股力量交織之下，企業面對的不再是單一威脅，而是速度與範圍同時擴張的攻擊環境。卡巴斯基臺灣技術總監謝長軒指出，AI能大量產出資料，決定防禦成敗的關鍵，不是誰握有最多預警訊號，而是誰能把海量資料轉化為可以立即行動的情報。 他認為，好的威脅情報必須同時具備來源可信、時間有效、脈絡相關、信心度清楚與可執行等條件，AI能加快前段處理，專家則負責高風險判斷與情境分析，兩者缺一不可。

items.title: 日本IDC Frontier雲端遭勒索軟體攻擊，波及495家客戶、部分系統靠備份重建
items.summary: 日本雲端服務業者IDC Frontier旗下IDCF Cloud於10月7日遭勒索軟體攻擊，造成部分虛擬伺服器停機且無法重新啟動，影響495個企業及地方政府客戶。IDC Frontier在8日指出，受影響服務區的客戶資料恐難以取出或復原，目前研判只能透過客戶自行保存的備份重建系統。
